edbDesc: A visual phenomenon caused by aliasing that occurs when continuous motion is represented by a series of short or instantaneous samples. It occurs when the view of a moving object is represented by a series of short samples as distinct from a continuous view, and the moving object is in rotational or other cyclic motion at a rate close to the sampling rate.
title: Stroboscopic effect
description: A spinning wheel lit by a flashing light seems to stand still, or creep slowly backwards, when the flashes keep pace with its turning. Plateau and Stampfer built spinning slotted discs around it in 1832, and mechanics still use it to read the speed of engines and machines without touching them.
effect: flashing light makes fast repeating motion look frozen or slowed
usedIn: Timing lights for setting car engine ignition
strength: A strobe flashing a few thousand times a minute can freeze a fan or engine part spinning at the same speed so it can be read like a still picture.
pickWhy: Specific named effect that measures and inspects motion; Faraday described a related wheel illusion in 1831, but the stroboscope itself is Plateau and Stampfer's.
